description: 57% of households food insecure, about 80% aid recipients, 34.5% unemployment among those able and willing to work - one of the highest rates in the world.
energy_note: The numbers are real. The explanation offered is not.

description: A fishery restricted to 15% of its water, a manufacturing sector without electricity, a workforce without permits and an import regime that bans pumps, will produce exactly these figures in any population on earth.
energy_note: Any people, under this, would show these numbers.

aspect: And aid dependency is then held against them
description: Receiving aid is treated as a disposition rather than an outcome, which supports the argument for restricting the aid, which deepens the dependency.
energy_note: Blamed for needing what you were made to need.

aspect: This is the bridge into the psychological section
description: Everything in PSY rests on this row: the conditions are imposed, the resulting statistics are attributed to the character of the people, and the person then carries that attribution into every room she enters abroad.
energy_note: Carrying a reputation manufactured by a blockade.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the figures that get quoted without their cause
description: 57% of Gaza households food insecure, about 80% aid recipients, 34.5% unemployment among those able and willing to work. The fishery was restricted to 15% of its water, manufacturing had 5-7 hours of power, and water and sewage pumps were on the restricted-import list.
energy_note: The statistics, and the policy that produced them, in one row.
